**In one line**: XDA reports that Linus Torvalds said he "really likes using AI" while the Linux developer community debates rules for LLM-generated contributions.

### Key points
- The Linux community is debating how to handle code and other content produced by large language models.
- Linus Torvalds, who created the Linux kernel, reportedly spoke favorably about using AI tools himself.
- Judging by the headline, his remarks lean toward allowing AI use rather than restricting it. The details of the proposed rules and the full context of his comments are in the original report.

### Why it matters
Other open-source projects often take their lead on contribution policy from the Linux kernel. Positive comments about AI from its most influential maintainer could shape how other large projects write their own AI contribution rules.
